item.title: Brazil elections: Can Lula’s anti-poverty record win over voters?
item.description: In Brazil, incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is seeking a fourth and final term in the presidential election on October 4. In 2022, he made the fight against hunger and poverty a key campaign promise. Between 2023 and 2024, nearly nine million people were lifted out of poverty thanks to the government’s social and economic programs. The decline was particularly sharp in Brazil’s Northeast. A traditional stronghold for Lula, will the progress made in reducing poverty translate into stronger support for the current president? FRANCE 24's team on the ground reports. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Burnham reopens Brexit debate: EU says UK must chart Its own path on future relations
item.description: The EU said Wednesday it was up to London to chart a way forward for Britain's relations with the bloc, after Prime Minister Andy Burnham put the idea of rejoining on the table. Burnham reopened the divisive Brexit debate Wednesday by saying his centre-left Labour government could go "all the way" and propose membership of the bloc, once it has weighed the "pros and cons" of different possible relationships with Europe. For the European perspective, FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Prisoners freed early in England and Wales risk living on the streets, say probation officers
item.description: Warning of a lack of hostel places for 2,000 criminals due to be released over the next month to ease overcrowding Hundreds of prisoners are due to be released early from jail on Thursday amid warnings that many will have nowhere to live and the probation system will struggle to monitor them. About 2,000 criminals including domestic abusers and violent offenders are to be freed over the next month, with another 3,000 in stages over the next year to ease overcrowding. The number was reduced from 6,000 after an intervention by the prime minister , Andy Burnham. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Netanyahu felicita a pasajero del vuelo Dubái-Tel Aviv que ayudó a neutralizar al copiloto
item.description: Tras horas de tensión, los pasajeros del vuelo FZ1073 de Flydubai regresaron a Israel, donde fueron recibidos entre aplausos y celebraciones. El primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu felicitó a uno de los viajeros que ayudó a neutralizar al copiloto señalado de desatar el caos a bordo, destacando que su actuación contribuyó a evitar una tragedia. Según las autoridades israelíes, el incidente fue un posible "intento de atentado terrorista yihadista". El avión, que cubría la ruta Dubái-Tel Aviv, realizó un aterrizaje de emergencia en Arabia Saudita y los hechos siguen bajo investigación. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: España debate dos decretos clave sobre vivienda; Sánchez se muestra "optimista"

El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, se mostró "razonablemente optimista" sobre la aprobación en el Congreso de dos decretos destinados a afrontar la crisis habitacional. Las iniciativas incluyen medidas contra los desahucios, cambios en los alquileres y otras herramientas para facilitar el acceso a la vivienda. La votación llega tras una creciente presión social y grandes protestas por la falta de soluciones habitacionales asequibles. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Transport suspended in some French cities as school protests continue
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu convened a crisis meeting Thursday as students staged new protests against understaffing, onerous schedules and overheated classrooms, with public transport affected in several cities. More than 600 people, most of them students, have been detained and dozens of police injured amid the increasingly violent protests. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: Donald Trump has launched “America”, an AI chatbot designed as a digital portal for US government information. But its responses appear to be changing. item.description: A partir de este miércoles 30 de septiembre, Estados Unidos elimina los viajes educativos grupales y refuerza las restricciones financieras sobre la isla. La Habana respondió, acusando a la Administración del presidente Donald Trump de intentar frenar sus reformas económicas. Entretanto, China asegura que “no se quedará de brazos cruzados” ante la crisis cubana. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24
